note: The kit theme registry (#1852 Phase 3) — the ONE source of truth for the SDK's THEME axis. A theme is a map of overrides for the contracted tokens (the base palette `--bg-*`/`--fg-*`/`--border*`/`--accent*` and the semantic component tokens `--card-*`/`--btn-*`/`--field-*`/`--chip-*`, all defined in src-tauri/data/ui/tokens-contract.css), plus an optional `base` ("dark"|"light") naming the SURFACE the theme sits on. Applying a theme sets the token overrides — globally on :root (via appearance/useAppBoot, same mechanism as the accent) or scoped on a subtree (via <ThemeScope>, for a coexisting themed card or an isolated live preview); the Design Studio preview additionally reads `base` to pick its sandbox surface. This file is read by BOTH faces: the frontend (`src/shared/ui/kit/theme.ts` loads it + applies it) AND `bsc ui theme list|get` (crates/bsc-ui embeds it), so a live agent can enumerate + read themes from its own shell. Every theme declares its DESIGN GROUP via a REQUIRED `tech` slug (#2749) — the same `tech` axis a kit carries (react, vue, …); the relationship is mandatory and 1:1 from the theme's side (a theme belongs to exactly one design group, a group hosts its own set of themes), so `bsc ui theme set`/`validate` reject a theme with no `tech` and the Themes page groups by it. React is the only design group today, so every packaged palette is `"tech": "react"`. `Dark` (empty overrides) is the base look; `Light` is the same look on the light surface; the named palettes are recognizable, permissively-licensed open-source color schemes (Nord, Dracula, Solarized, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night, Monokai) that rebind the WHOLE base palette — every value is a literal color so a palette composes cleanly over the contract without depending on the chosen accent.
